title: Why Do LLMs Accept Generics? Explaining Acceptability using Psycholinguistic and Model-Derived Factors
abstract: arXiv:2610.27928v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Psycholinguistic studies explore why humans accept some generic statements but reject others by showing that these judgments depend on more than how common a property is. People consider several other factors such as how well it sets the kind apart from others or whether it is characteristic of the kind.   Inspired by the linguistic and cognitive literature, we explore to what extent factors from these studies explain how large language models (LLMs) judge generics. Our results with twelve models on a psycholinguistic dataset and on naturally occurring generics show that models weigh how common a property is against how well it distinguishes the kind, and combine the two much as people do, though less clearly. Like people, they favor characteristic properties, but unlike the accounts of human judgment, they ignore striking ones. What matters most to LLMs is whether a statement is factually true, and much of the influence of human factors

translated_title: 为什么大语言模型会接受泛指句？利用心理语言学与模型衍生因素解释可接受性
translated_abstract: 心理语言学研究探讨了为什么人类会接受某些泛指句而拒绝另一些泛指句，并表明这些判断不仅取决于某种属性的普遍程度，人们还会考虑其他多种因素，例如该属性能否很好地将这一类别与其他类别区分开来，或者该属性是否是该类别的典型特征。受语言学和认知科学文献的启发，我们探讨了这些研究中的因素能在多大程度上解释大语言模型对泛指句的判断。我们在一个心理语言学数据集和自然出现的泛指句上对十二个模型进行了实验，结果表明，模型会权衡属性的普遍性与属性区分类别的能力，并以与人类相似的方式将二者结合起来，尽管这种结合不如人类那样清晰。与人类一样，模型也偏好典型属性，但与人类判断的相关解释不同的是，它们会忽略引人注目的属性。对大语言模型而言，最重要的是陈述在事实上是否为真，而人类相关因素的很大一部分影响
tldr: 该研究首次利用心理语言学因素（属性普遍性、区分性、典型性）和模型衍生因素系统解释了大语言模型判断泛指句可接受性的机制，发现模型像人类一样权衡属性普遍性与区分性并偏好典型属性，但与人类不同，它们忽略引人注目的属性，而最看重陈述的事实真实性。
en_tdlr: This study explains how LLMs judge the acceptability of generic statements using psycholinguistic and model-derived factors, finding that models combine property prevalence and distinctiveness like humans do and favor characteristic properties, but unlike humans they ignore striking properties and prioritize factual truth above all else.
